note: Which of this engine's public core exports anything outside core actually calls, and which ones are recorded as isolated. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-358 retired six families of unconsumed core surface by hand, one module at a time, because nothing measured the gap: the barrel could grow a symbol nobody outside core ever called and every gate stayed green. platform-doctor's unusedExports leg reads this file and turns red on a symbol with no consumer that is not recorded below, and on a recorded entry that has since gained a consumer or whose symbol no longer exists. The second half is what keeps this file a register rather than an amnesty: the leg makes an entry leave the moment its debt is paid. It does not refuse a new entry -- recording an isolated symbol here is one of the three ways its own remedy names to go green -- so this list shrinking is a review obligation, not a machine one.
consumerRootsRationale: The three surfaces the charter names as consumers of core: the CLI, the host hooks, and the portal. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-363 names one more file, scripts/backfill-work-summaries.mjs: it is the one-shot chain-write tool that gives the records predating the summary field one, and it derives each summary by calling core's deriveWorkSummary rather than by carrying a second copy of the rule. It is listed as a single file, not as scripts/, so the widening admits exactly the one consumer it was opened for. Test files under these roots are excluded by the leg itself rather than by this list -- a symbol whose only caller is its own test is the shape STORY-358 spent an Epic removing, and admitting tests would have reported every one of those modules as consumed on the day before it was deleted. Widening this list is the way to make a red result green without connecting anything, which is exactly why it is written down here instead of being compiled into the leg; no verb checks who widened it, so a widening is judged in review. TCRN-CROSS-STORY-364 names one more file on the same terms, scripts/knowledge-language.mjs: it is the one-shot migration executor that gives the cards written before the artefact-language policy existed their translated fields and their phrasings, and it decides both by calling core's detectLanguage and applyWriteLanguagePolicy through the barrel rather than by carrying a second copy of the rule. It is listed as a single file, not as scripts/, so the widening admits exactly the one consumer it was opened for. regeneration: Empty allowedUnconsumed, run node scripts/platform-doctor.mjs --platform-root <container>, and the red result's unconsumedWithoutAllowance is the measured set. There is no generator script: a second implementation of this measurement is a second answer waiting to disagree with the leg's.

The leg forces an entry out the moment its symbol is retired or gains a consumer; it does not refuse a new one, so keeping this list moving down is a review obligation rather than a machine one. Retiring these is the work the charter's isolation rule schedules, not work this Story does -- STORY-358 showed each family costs its own barrel edit, its own registry updates and its own gate round, and doing 484 of them in the Story that installs the meter would have buried the meter.
